title: observability: add token-level KV & cost/latency metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: recurring oncall noise and cost surprises from route-level KV cache behavior plus poor visibility into per-token cost and latency breakdowns. This PR adds token-level metrics (cost and latency per token group), expands KV cache visibility (hits/misses by model/route/tenant), hooks tracing spans for cache lookup and kernel selection, ships a Grafana dashboard with new panels, and updates alert thresholds to reduce false positives while preserving SLO coverage.

What this PR does: Adds new metrics (token_cost_usd_total, token_latency_ms_bucketed, kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_route, token_emit_count_by_model), instruments critical runtime paths (prefix cache lookup, KV fetch, kernel selection) with lightweight spans, and exports a summarized rollup for low-cardinality dashboards. Adds a Grafana dashboard JSON (observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json), alerting rules (observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml) with tuned thresholds and suppression rules, and observability docs (docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md). Includes unit and integration tests for metric labels and a lightweight smoke test for the dashboard provisioning job.

Backwards compatibility and cost: All new metrics are additive and guarded behind a config flag (REDWOOD_OBS_TOKEN_LEVEL=true). Default remains off for tenants that opt out. Metric cardinality is controlled: detailed tags (request_id/session_id) are not added, and rollups are emitted at 1m granularity to avoid cardinality explosion.

Testing and rollout: CI runs unit tests and a staging integration that enables the flag for a small fleet. Alerts were tuned in collaboration with SRE to avoid flapping; we add a 15m suppression window for model rollout churn and a separate high-severity alert for sudden cost spikes that bypass suppression.

Notes: this PR references ENG-3421 (token-level cost monitoring) and SUP-1187 (customer-reported cost spike incident). For rollout, we will enable REDWOOD_OBS_TOKEN_LEVEL in a canary subset, monitor increased metric ingestion, and gradually expand.
